newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate down to 11.5 from 12.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate down to 11.5 from 12.7 pct.

text.p: A higher volume of short-term loans granted at lower prices pushed the Croatian average lending rate down on Friday to 11.5 from 12.7 percent amid continued strained liquidity, dealers said.
"The cheaper short-term loans have accounted for a much larger share of today's trade, so the weighted rate went down," dealer Jasenka Blagaic told Reuters.
Daily settlements totalled 70 million kuna with borrowers seeking another 15 million.
Fresh trade was put at 46.5 million kuna, two thirds of it call money loans granted at a weighted rate of 10.9 percent.
Term deals were struck at between 10 and 11 percent for four-day funds and 18 percent for 90-day borrowings.
Insurers rolled over previous loans at steady nine percent for one-week funds and 16 percent for call money borrowings.
Banks charged 10.5 percent for old call money loans, 13 percent for one-week funds and 17 percent for 20-day borrowings.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Saturday and Monday weaker at 6.0729 against the dollar and flat at 3.5725 against the German mark. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
